brief.scope:
Review the watchdog backlog fix and the watch skill, slice one (PR #244, lane/session-20260916-f, head 515e5b72). Contract: ops/conductor/watchdog-lever.md.
Aim skepticism at: the ruling that a watcher reports nothing about what it can see at start (closed records, no-copy directories, unreadable inputs) unless --report-existing is given, and only what changes after start speaks; the claim that no live condition changed, pinned by a test that plants a directory after start; the contract wording that replaced the old carve-out; the class-level fixture override adding --report-existing to planted-closed families; and whether .claude/skills/watch/SKILL.md tells a session anything the tools and contracts do not measure.

caps.turns_note: codex offers no turn-cap flag (measured 2026-09-12: its --help names none); caps.turns is recorded, the wall cap governs

findings.claim: startup_silent permanently suppresses an ID, not merely its startup condition. A no-copy directory whose record.json becomes unreadable after startup emits neither deviation unavailable nor watchdog error, and a startup-closed record amended to introduce a deviation is never rescanned. This contradicts watchdog-lever.md:57-60 and :223-225. The new live test only plants an entirely new ID, so it misses both transitions.
findings.reproduce: Using test_watchdog._WatchdogFixture, plant_no_copy(ID), start loop(), then mkdir ID/record.json after 0.2s: measured ERROR_LINES=[] and DEVIATIONS=[]. Separately plant a closed-ok record and amend it after start to closed-tripped with changed_paths: measured DEVIATIONS=[].

findings.claim: The advertised "stalls, deviations, CI" Monitor command cannot report CI: it passes --no-forge, which prevents CI acquisition, and its grep expression does not match lines beginning "ci fail" or "ci cancel".
findings.reproduce: printf '%s\n' 'ci fail #244 at 0123456789012345678901234567890123456789: lane' 'stall lane/x: no dispatch running, 60 min since the lock' | grep -E --line-buffered 'stall |deviation |no record copy |harness gone |watchdog error' outputs only the stall line.

findings.claim: The old-checkout awk fallback discards live conditions whenever their line contains a prior-day record ID. Stall lines commonly name the closed record anchoring the stall, contrary to line 87's claim that stall names no record; long, unobservable, and harness-gone lines can be lost similarly.
findings.reproduce: printf '%s\n' 'stall lane/x: no dispatch running, 60 min since 20260915T090000Z-code-test-old' | awk -v today=20260916 '$0 !~ /[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z/ || $0 ~ today {print; fflush()}' produces no output.

findings.claim: The skill makes the exact Monitor(...) API, per-stdout-line chat delivery, and 30-minute ceiling load-bearing without a current contract or probe. The capability inventory only measures generic background-task completion notifications, while repository search finds the exact Monitor surface only in this new skill and a historical proposal. A session therefore cannot distinguish unsupported delivery from a quiet watch.
findings.reproduce: rg -n 'Monitor\(|timeout_ms|stdout line.*message|30 minutes' ops/devlane/harness ops/conductor/harness-capabilities.md .claude/skills/watch/SKILL.md ops/conductor/mcp-tools.md

findings.claim: Both user-facing flag descriptions retain the old meaning, saying --report-existing reports records already closed at startup. The revised contract also makes startup no-copy and unreadable directories backlog, so help omits two condition families the flag now controls.
findings.reproduce: python3 ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py --help | sed -n '/report-existing/,+1p' prints 'report records already closed at start'.
